query: Which staggered‑DiD estimators and event‑study windows will we pre‑specify to handle heterogeneous treatment timing?

response.query: Which staggered‑DiD estimators and event‑study windows will we pre‑specify to handle heterogeneous treatment timing?
response.answer: For heterogeneous treatment timing, use staggered-DiD estimators with flexible event-study windows ranging from -5 to +5 periods around treatment initiation. Pre-specify windows based on treatment group differences.

results.content: The chapter builds on the framework outlined in the *OECD Recommendation on Ageing and Employment Policies* [(OECD, 2022[4])](/en/publications/2025/07/oecd-employment-outlook-2025_5345f034/full-report/component-7.html#Mend_3fjdRRRL1DeJuGWi4O1t8g_8cc632ab68) and *Working Better with Age* [(OECD, 2019[5])](/en/publications/2025/07/oecd-employment-outlook-2025_5345f034/full-report/component-7.html#Kapp_c4d4f66a_8cc632ab68) and argues that greater efforts are needed to promote the labour market inclusion of older workers, especially in countries where employment rates lag behind among particular groups of older workers. In evaluating pension reforms in 2010 in France which raised the statutory retirement age (SEA) from 60 to 62, Rabaté and Rochut [(2020[143])](/en/publications/2025/07/oecd-employment-outlook-2025_5345f034/full-report/component-7.html#Mendeley_QbdeQUkVpz__D_DtXC0gAxA_8cc632ab68) show that while the reform significantly increased employment rates among older workers, it also led to a rise in unemployment and disability claims. A study of nine OECD countries found that phased retirement results in a slight increase in labour force participation and a decline in the number of hours worked, leading to no significant overall boost in labour supply [(Börsch-Supan et al., 2018[144])](/en/publications/2025/07/oecd-employment-outlook-2025_5345f034/full-report/component-7.html#Mendeley_Kj5HTIE8LzO1BG8wAdG__Zg_8cc632ab68).
